title: LangPrecip: Language-Aware Multimodal Precipitation Nowcasting
claim: Vision-only prediction leaves future motion ambiguous and misses extreme events; adding language constraints resolves ambiguity and yields clearly better results.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: failing baseline, ours, bar chart; dashed divider
description: The figure has two side-by-side contrasting panels and a result inset. Panel A, on a pink background, is titled Visual-Only Forecasting. It shows four radar frames (T-4 to T-1) feeding a branching arrow set labeled Path A, Path B and Path C, with a question mark and a note that visual patterns alone cannot determine the motion. A red arrow leads to a blurry predicted future with a red X and the label Extreme Event Failure. Panel B, on a green background, is titled LangPrecip. It shows the same radar frames plus a Motion Description text box with color-highlighted words. A blue arrow labeled as navigation constraining the motion leads to a sharp prediction with a green check and the label Extreme Event Success. At right, a red dashed box holds a bar chart: Visual-Only 0.046 against LangPrecip 0.074 CSI, with +60% in red.
caption: Visual-only nowcasting suffers from motion ambiguity under limited radar history. LangPrecip resolves this ambiguity by using language-based motion descriptions to constrain precipitation evolution and improve extreme event prediction.
abstract: Short-term precipitation nowcasting is an inherently uncertain and under-constrained spatiotemporal forecasting problem, especially for rapidly evolving and extreme weather events. Existing generative approaches rely primarily on visual conditioning, leaving future motion weakly constrained and ambiguous. We propose a language-aware multimodal nowcasting framework(LangPrecip) that treats meteorological text as a semantic motion constraint on precipitation evolution. By formulating nowcasting as a semantically constrained trajectory generation problem under the Rectified Flow paradigm, our method enables efficient and physically consistent integration of textual and radar information in latent space.We further introduce LangPrecip-160k, a large-scale multimodal dataset with 160k paired radar sequences and motion descriptions. Experiments on Swedish and MRMS datasets show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, achieving over 60 \% and 19\% gains in heavy-rainfall CSI at an 80-minute lead time.
